findings.title: http reachable on port 80
findings.detail: Web admin over cleartext. Credentials cross the network in the clear.
findings.remediation: Disable the service if unused, or restrict it to a management VLAN / VPN with a firewall rule. Cameras should never expose admin or control ports to an untrusted network.

findings.title: dahua-dvrip reachable on port 37777
findings.detail: Dahua DVRIP control port. Should not face untrusted networks.
findings.remediation: Disable the service if unused, or restrict it to a management VLAN / VPN with a firewall rule. Cameras should never expose admin or control ports to an untrusted network.

findings.title: Possibly affected: Authentication bypass via crafted login (ONVIF/NetKeyboard)
findings.detail: Check the Dahua PSIRT advisory for the fixed build for your exact model. (applies to this vendor; confirm your exact model/build against the advisory).
findings.remediation: Update to the vendor's fixed firmware and, until then, remove the device's exposure to untrusted networks.

findings.title: Possibly affected: Authentication bypass via crafted login packet
findings.detail: Companion advisory to CVE-2021-33044. Apply the vendor's fixed build. (applies to this vendor; confirm your exact model/build against the advisory).
findings.remediation: Update to the vendor's fixed firmware and, until then, remove the device's exposure to untrusted networks.

findings.title: Firmware version could not be determined
findings.detail: The device did not expose its firmware version to an unauthenticated request.
findings.remediation: Check the firmware version in the admin UI and compare it against the vendor's security advisories.

findings.title: dvrip-xmeye reachable on port 34567
findings.detail: Generic DVRIP/XMEye port, tied to many botnet-recruited DVRs.
findings.remediation: Disable the service if unused, or restrict it to a management VLAN / VPN with a firewall rule. Cameras should never expose admin or control ports to an untrusted network.

findings.title: Port 34567 advisory
findings.detail: DVRIP/XMEye (port 34567) DVRs are a frequent Mirai/botnet target. If you do not use the XMEye cloud, disable it and block the port.
findings.remediation: Disable the service/cloud feature and block the port at the firewall.

findings.remediation: Check the firmware version in the admin UI and compare it against the vendor's security advisories.

findings.title: Improper authentication: backdoor allowing config/credential disclosure
findings.detail: Elevated access to device config without valid credentials on old firmware. (firmware 5.4.0 is below the fixed version 5.4.5).
findings.remediation: Update to the vendor's fixed firmware and, until then, remove the device's exposure to untrusted networks.

findings.title: Unauthenticated command injection in the web server
findings.detail: Widely exploited. Update firmware and restrict the web interface immediately. (firmware 5.4.0 is below the fixed version 5.5.800).
findings.remediation: Update to the vendor's fixed firmware and, until then, remove the device's exposure to untrusted networks.

findings.title: Factory-default credentials still accepted
findings.detail: The device accepted the documented default login 'admin:12345'. Anyone who can reach it can log in.
findings.remediation: Set a unique strong password now, disable unused accounts, and enable lockout on repeated failures.

findings.title: telnet reachable on port 23
findings.detail: Cleartext remote shell. Should never be open on a camera.
findings.remediation: Disable the service if unused, or restrict it to a management VLAN / VPN with a firewall rule. Cameras should never expose admin or control ports to an untrusted network.

findings.title: Port 23 advisory
findings.detail: Telnet on cameras has historically shipped with hard-coded credentials (e.g. the Mirai default-password list). Disable it.
findings.remediation: Disable the service/cloud feature and block the port at the firewall.
